name: Scandinavian Urethroplasty Study
question: Does buccal mucosa graft urethroplasty cause fewer penile complications or less erectile dysfunction than transecting excision and primary anastomosis for short bulbar strictures?

design.population: Patients aged 18 to 70 years with a bulbar urethral stricture of 2 cm or less and no previous open urethroplasty (median age 35 years, median stricture length 10 mm).

verdictNote: Penile complications favored graft; IIEF-5 did not differ; enrollment stopped at 151 of 300 planned.
takeaway: In men with bulbar urethral strictures of 2 cm or less, buccal mucosa graft urethroplasty was followed by fewer patient-reported penile complications than transecting excision and primary anastomosis at 12 months (16% versus 33%); IIEF-5 scores and recurrence (12.9% overall) did not differ.

reports.label: Initial 12-month report
reports.citation: Nilsen OJ, Holm HV, Ekerhult TO, et al. To Transect or Not Transect: Results from the Scandinavian Urethroplasty Study, A Multicentre Randomised Study of Bulbar Urethroplasty Comparing Excision and Primary Anastomosis Versus Buccal Mucosal Grafting. *Eur Urol.* 2022;81(4):375-382.
reports.followUp: 12 months; 144/151 completed the 12-month visit; final follow-up visit 9 February 2021

results.measure: One or more penile complications on the penile complications questionnaire (PCQ questions 2 to 5: glans filling, glans sensation, penile length, penile direction) at 12 months; risk difference (tEPA minus BMG), percentage points
results.note: Prespecified primary endpoint, patient-reported on a questionnaire designed for this study and not validated; the prespecified metric was an odds ratio, and the report gives risk differences with a chi-square test. P values were not corrected for multiple testing; enrollment was 151 of 300 planned.

results.measure: Mean IIEF-5 score at 12 months; between-arm difference from analysis of covariance
results.note: Table 5 gives the difference as 1.2 without stating its direction; the arm means are 23.0 (BMG) and 21.8 (tEPA). Median preoperative IIEF-5 was 25 in both arms.
results.locator: PDF p5, Table 5; journal p379; baseline PDF p3, Table 3

results.measure: One or more penile complications (PCQ questions 2 to 5) at 3 months; risk difference (tEPA minus BMG), percentage points
results.note: Same questionnaire and analysis as the primary endpoint.

results.measure: PCQ question 2 'yes' (less stiffness of the penis head during erection) at 12 months; risk difference (tEPA minus BMG), percentage points
results.note: Component of the primary penile-complication endpoint.

results.measure: PCQ question 4 'yes' (erect penis has become shorter) at 12 months; risk difference (tEPA minus BMG), percentage points
results.note: Component of the primary penile-complication endpoint.

results.measure: PCQ question 3 'yes' (lost feeling in the head of the penis) at 12 months; risk difference (tEPA minus BMG), percentage points
results.note: Component of the primary penile-complication endpoint.

results.measure: PCQ question 5 'yes' (erect penis points in a different direction) at 12 months; risk difference (tEPA minus BMG), percentage points
results.note: Reported at 3 months in 0 of the BMG arm and 7 (10%) of the tEPA arm (p = 0.005).

results.measure: PCQ question 1 'yes' (ejaculation has become worse) at 3 months; risk difference (tEPA minus BMG), percentage points
results.note: Question 1 was excluded from the one-or-more-complications analysis because the authors did not consider ejaculation a penile problem.

results.measure: PCQ question 1 'yes' (ejaculation has become worse) at 12 months; risk difference (tEPA minus BMG), percentage points
Mean IIEF-5 score at 3 months; between-arm difference from analysis of covariance
results.note: Table 5 gives the difference as 1.2 without stating its direction.

results.measure: Recurrence, defined as need for additional surgery, within 12-month follow-up; risk difference (tEPA minus BMG), percentage points
results.note: Recurrence data were available for 147 patients; 19 (12.9%) had a recurrence overall. Lumen patency was not assessed by endoscopy or urethrography at follow-up, and the trial was not designed or powered to detect a recurrence difference.
Mean difference 1 mL/s (95% CI -4 to 6); the table does not state its direction. Median preoperative maximum flow was 9 mL/s (BMG) and 8 mL/s (tEPA).

results.note: Mean difference 17 mL (95% CI -10 to 44); the table does not state its direction. Median preoperative residual volume was 90 mL (BMG) and 67 mL (tEPA).
results.locator: PDF p5, Table 6; journal p379; PDF p3, Table 3

harms.label: Postoperative bleeding (scrotal or perineal hematoma)
harms.note: Risk difference (tEPA minus BMG) 20 percentage points (95% CI 9 to 31); p < 0.001. All were Clavien-Dindo grade I except three tEPA patients (one grade II, one IIIa, one IIIb).

harms.label: Wound infection after discharge or at catheter removal
harms.locator: PDF pp4-5, section 3.4 and Table 7; journal pp378-379
harms.note: Grade II in two and grade IIIa in one of the three tEPA patients; none at 3 or 12 months in either arm.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection at 12 months
harms.note: All grade I to II; no significant differences between arms. At catheter removal 6/76 (7.9%) after BMG versus 1/75 (1.3%) after tEPA; at 3 months 3/74 (4.1%) versus 2/71 (2.8%); postoperatively 2/76 (2.6%) versus 0/75.

harms.label: Contrast leakage on urethrography at catheter removal
harms.note: Eight of 136 patients examined, with no difference between groups. In all eight the catheter stayed another 2 weeks; it was then removed without repeat urethrography in six, and urethrography in the other two showed no leakage.

harms.label: Perineal or lower-extremity pain, anesthesia or dysesthesia
harms.note: Six patients early postoperatively, ten at 3 months and three at 12 months, all grade I to II.

harms.label: Myocardial infarction
harms.note: One patient, 6 days after surgery, required coronary stenting (grade IVa). No deep venous thrombosis or compartment syndrome.

harms.label: Oral discomfort after graft harvest

values.exp: 26 (34%) during the hospital stay; 4 (5.2%) at catheter removal; 3 (3.9%) at 3 and at 12 months

harms.note: In-hospital discomfort was mild in 15 and moderate in 11; later reports were all mild.

harms.label: Donor-site bleeding, Stensen duct occlusion or donor-site infection

values.exp: 1 (1.3%) bleeding, grade I; no duct occlusion or infection

delivery.label: Randomized and operated as assigned
delivery.note: Three patients (2%) were not operated as assigned: two randomized to tEPA had BMG because of unexpectedly long strictures (one with an augmented end-to-end anastomosis) and one randomized to BMG had tEPA. Analysis was by intention to treat.

delivery.label: Graft position in BMG operations
delivery.note: Position followed surgeon preference; a subgroup analysis showed no difference in penile complications between dorsal and ventral grafts.

delivery.label: tEPA technique
delivery.value: Transection of the corpus spongiosum and excision of the stricture, with two-layer anastomosis.
delivery.note: The participating centers agreed the operative techniques before the study started.

delivery.label: BMG technique
delivery.value: Corpus spongiosum incised along the length of the stricture, ventrally or dorsally, with a buccal mucosa graft placed on the urethral defect; no transection.

delivery.label: Postoperative care
delivery.value: Indwelling Foley catheter for 2 to 3 weeks with antibiotic treatment and antithrombotic prophylaxis; postoperative treatment was the same for both groups at each center.
delivery.note: Antibiotics, antithrombotic prophylaxis and physical limitations were at each center's discretion.

delivery.label: Planned versus achieved enrollment
delivery.locator: PDF pp2,6, sections 2.3 and 4.1; journal pp376,380
delivery.note: The target gave 80% power at an alpha of 0.05 for 30% versus 15% penile complications with 134 per group. Inclusion stopped after more than 4 years, without interim analysis, because reaching the target would have taken 8 to 10 years.

delivery.label: Follow-up completion
delivery.value: 144 completed 12-month follow-up; 4 lost to follow-up and 3 left the study because of early stricture recurrence.
delivery.note: PCQ data were available for 139 patients at 3 months and 144 at 12 months; IIEF-5 for 150 preoperatively, 137 at 3 months and 142 at 12 months.
